summary: Add connector troubleshooting UI and strongly typed reusable canvas contracts
description:
h2. Background

Apache NiFi supports a TROUBLESHOOTING connector state, but the frontend does not yet provide the complete workflow for entering, using, and ending that state.

Troubleshooting mode should provide controlled access to a connector's managed process group so operators can diagnose and correct problems without treating the connector as normally running. Stronger reusable-canvas contracts are also needed to support these editing operations safely.
h2. Goals
 * Allow users to enter and end connector troubleshooting mode.
 * Keep connector listings, details, canvas state, and navigation synchronized with state transitions.
 * Expose troubleshooting operations on the managed process group.
 * Restrict advanced routes and operations based on connector state and permissions.
 * Replace permissive canvas entity types with canonical NiFi entity contracts.
 * Keep frontend interaction metadata separate from REST write payloads.

h2. Scope

Troubleshooting functionality includes:
 * Enter and end troubleshooting actions.
 * Troubleshooting state presentation and explanatory banners.
 * Polling and navigation behavior that reacts to connector state changes.
 * Route protection for advanced troubleshooting pages.
 * Component run-status operations.
 * Processor advanced UI access.
 * Connector-scoped Controller Service editing.
 * Remote Process Group refresh.
 * Horizontal and vertical alignment.
 * Provenance replay where supported.
 * Permission and connector-state gating.

Canvas typing includes:
 * Canonical TypeScript models for NiFi component entities.
 * Typed connector-canvas state, actions, reducers, effects, and service boundaries.
 * Typed reusable-canvas wrappers, selections, render contexts, and gestures.
 * Separate response-entity and write-payload contracts.
 * Narrow connection endpoint serialization matching NiFi REST DTOs.
 * Removal of permissive entity any and unknown types from migrated canvas paths.

h2. Out of Scope
 * Changes to backend troubleshooting lifecycle semantics.
 * Migration of the legacy flow-designer implementation onto the reusable canvas.
 * Unrelated connector configuration or deployment workflows.

h2. Acceptance Criteria
 * Users can enter and end troubleshooting mode when the corresponding backend action is allowed.
 * The UI consistently represents TROUBLESHOOTING and reacts to state transitions without a manual reload.
 * Advanced troubleshooting routes reject connectors outside troubleshooting mode.
 * Canvas and Controller Service operations require the appropriate connector state and permissions.
 * Troubleshooting banners clearly identify the active mode.
 * Canonical canvas entities match the NiFi Java DTO and resource contracts.
 * Connection create and reconnect requests contain only the expected NiFi endpoint fields.
 * Migrated production canvas paths do not use permissive entity any types.
 * Unit tests cover lifecycle actions, route guards, permissions, state transitions, operations, and API payload boundaries.
 * Frontend lint, type-check, tests, and production build pass.

summary: Define canonical TypeScript entity and request contracts for canvas components
description:
h2. Background

The connector canvas currently stores component collections as any[] and relies on loosely typed objects across state, rendering, and interaction boundaries. Several copies of shared primitives such as Position also exist in separate canvas modules.

Before connector canvas editing is expanded, the frontend needs canonical TypeScript contracts that accurately represent NiFi REST response entities and write requests.

h2. Goals

* Establish one canonical TypeScript model for each canvas component entity.
* Consolidate shared canvas primitives.
* Distinguish server response entities from client write payloads.
* Model denied-read responses without weakening fields that NiFi always returns.
* Provide a stable type foundation for connector state and reusable-canvas work.

h2. Scope

h3. Shared Primitives

* Define a canonical Position interface in the shared library.
* Reuse the existing canonical Revision and Permissions interfaces.
* Replace duplicate Position declarations and update their consumers.
* Introduce RevisionRequest for write operations that do not include response-only revision fields.

h3. Entity Contracts

Add canonical response contracts for:

* ComponentEntityBase
* PositionableComponentEntityBase
* ProcessorEntity
* ConnectionEntity
* PortEntity
* ProcessGroupEntity
* RemoteProcessGroupEntity
* FunnelEntity
* LabelEntity

Include the component DTOs, status DTOs, and nested DTO contracts required to model these entities without any or open-ended index signatures.

h3. Request Contracts

Define typed request projections for canvas write operations, including:

* Component creation.
* Component position updates.
* Connection bend and label-index updates.
* Connection destination updates.
* Component run-status requests.
* Snippet-based move and delete operations.

Write contracts should derive field types from canonical response contracts with Pick, Omit, Partial, or equivalent utility types where practical. Response contracts must not be weakened to accommodate partial write bodies.

h2. Contract Rules

* Java DTOs, entity factories, and resource response behavior are the source of truth.
* Fields populated on every response are required.
* The component body is optional because it can be omitted when the user lacks read permission.
* Response-only fields must not appear in create or update request contracts.
* Dynamic index signatures such as [key: string]: unknown are not permitted on canonical entity contracts.
* Canvas entity contracts must not use explicit any.
* Connections remain non-positionable and use bends and labelIndex for geometry.
* Input and output ports share PortEntity and are distinguished by their port type.

h2. Out of Scope

* Migrating connector canvas state collections to the new entity contracts.
* Retyping reusable-canvas renderers and gestures.
* Changing REST endpoint behavior or Java DTOs.
* Changing connector troubleshooting behavior.
* Migrating the legacy flow-designer canvas.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A canonical shared Position type replaces the duplicate frontend definitions.
* Canonical response entities exist for all seven canvas component kinds.
* Entity requiredness matches NiFi resource and factory behavior.
* Unreadable entities can omit component while retaining the required envelope fields.
* Typed write contracts are separate from response entity contracts.
* Connection geometry and destination updates have dedicated typed payloads.
* No canonical entity contains explicit any or an open-ended index signature.
* Existing consumers compile after primitive consolidation.
* Type-focused tests or fixtures cover readable and unreadable entity shapes.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, and production build pass.

summary: Migrate connector canvas state and service boundaries to canonical entity types
description:
h2. Background

The connector canvas currently stores labels, funnels, ports, process groups, remote process groups, processors, and connections as any[]. Related actions, selectors, effects, and service responses also use permissive any types.

This prevents the compiler from validating API response handling and allows incorrect component shapes to propagate into the canvas.

h2. Goals

* Store each connector canvas collection using its canonical entity type.
* Type the connector flow service response.
* Remove permissive entity types from connector canvas state, actions, effects, reducers, and selectors.
* Preserve current loading, polling, navigation, selection, and sanitization behavior.
* Establish a typed state boundary for subsequent reusable-canvas work.

h2. Scope

h3. Connector Canvas State

Change the state collections to:

* labels: LabelEntity[]
* funnels: FunnelEntity[]
* inputPorts: PortEntity[]
* outputPorts: PortEntity[]
* remoteProcessGroups: RemoteProcessGroupEntity[]
* processGroups: ProcessGroupEntity[]
* processors: ProcessorEntity[]
* connections: ConnectionEntity[]

h3. Actions and Reducers

* Type loadConnectorFlowSuccess with concrete entity arrays.
* Type component-selection and component-configuration action payloads.
* Remove entity any usage from reducer inputs.
* Preserve collection replacement and route-change reset behavior.
* Ensure state updates remain immutable.

h3. Service Boundary

* Define ProcessGroupFlowEntity and FlowDTO response contracts.
* Change ConnectorService.getConnectorFlow() from Observable<any> to Observable<ProcessGroupFlowEntity>.
* Type the nested processGroupFlow, breadcrumb, parent group, and component collections.
* Type child input-port and output-port retrieval without Observable<any> or callback parameter casts.

h3. Effects and Selectors

* Remove collection casts from connector flow loading.
* Type position and bend sanitization helpers.
* Type entity-by-id selectors.
* Type connection cloning and bend copying.
* Type provenance eligibility and component-configuration lookups from the concrete entity union.
* Preserve polling and error handling behavior.

h3. Tests and Linting

* Add reusable typed factories for each connector canvas entity kind.
* Replace permissive test fixtures and action casts with the typed factories.
* Enable no-explicit-any for the migrated connector canvas state directory.
* Cover readable and unreadable component entities where relevant.

h2. Out of Scope

* Retyping reusable-canvas wrappers, renderers, and gesture handlers.
* Adding connector troubleshooting operations.
* Changing REST endpoint behavior.
* Changing canvas rendering or interaction behavior.
* Migrating the legacy flow-designer canvas.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* ConnectorCanvasState contains no any[] component collections.
* loadConnectorFlowSuccess uses concrete entity arrays.
* ConnectorService.getConnectorFlow() returns Observable<ProcessGroupFlowEntity>.
* Connector flow effects do not cast API collections to entity types.
* Connector canvas selectors do not use any callback parameters.
* Component configuration and provenance lookups use canonical entity types.
* Position and bend sanitization remain behaviorally unchanged and are fully typed.
* Existing polling, navigation, loading, and error behavior remains unchanged.
* Typed factories replace permissive fixtures in affected tests.
* no-explicit-any is enabled for the migrated state directory.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, and production build pass.

summary: Type reusable canvas wrappers, renderers, selections, and gesture contracts
description:
h2. Background

The reusable canvas wraps each server entity with frontend-only UI state for dimensions, selection, drag state, and rendering. These wrappers and many D3 renderer contracts currently use any, which prevents the compiler from validating entity access and interaction payloads.

The reusable canvas should use canonical entity contracts throughout its wrapper, rendering, selection, and gesture layers.

h2. Goals

* Type every reusable-canvas wrapper with its canonical entity.
* Introduce discriminated unions for canvas data and selected targets.
* Type D3 selections, render contexts, callbacks, and drag events.
* Separate frontend-only UI state from server-returned entity state.
* Type connection creation and endpoint-reconnection payloads.
* Eliminate explicit any from the reusable canvas directory.

h2. Scope

h3. Canvas Wrappers

Type each wrapper as:

* CanvasProcessor with ProcessorEntity.
* CanvasConnection with ConnectionEntity.
* CanvasPort with PortEntity.
* CanvasProcessGroup with ProcessGroupEntity.
* CanvasRemoteProcessGroup with RemoteProcessGroupEntity.
* CanvasFunnel with FunnelEntity.
* CanvasLabel with LabelEntity.

Retain frontend-only fields such as dimensions, current drag position, temporary bend state, preview state, and selection state under the wrapper's ui property.

h3. Canvas Data Union

* Replace the generic CanvasComponent shape with a discriminated CanvasDatum union.
* Use ui.componentType as the component-kind discriminator.
* Add narrowing helpers for processors, connections, named components, positionable components, and connectable components.
* Ensure labels and connections cannot participate as connection endpoints.

h3. Component Inputs and Outputs

* Type all reusable-canvas component collection inputs with concrete entity arrays.
* Type internal computed collections with the corresponding canvas wrappers.
* Type selection, context-menu, drag, resize, bend-point, label-index, connection-create, and reconnect outputs.
* Keep the reusable component independent of page-specific NgRx actions.

h3. Renderers and Layer Contracts

* Type each layer's D3 selections with the corresponding canvas wrapper.
* Replace renderer callback any parameters with shared callback aliases.
* Type render-context fields used by processor, connection, port, funnel, label, process-group, and remote-process-group renderers.
* Type D3 event subjects and currentTarget access without this aliases or unbounded casts.
* Scope D3 queries to the owning canvas instance.

h3. Selection Contracts

* Define a discriminated SelectionTarget union for context menus and bulk operations.
* Type clicked components, selected components, and related connections.
* Replace structural entity envelopes and nested any fields.
* Preserve route-based selection and context-menu behavior.

h3. Gesture Contracts

* Type the component drag pipeline and its drag-end baseline payload.
* Preserve the baseline revision captured at gesture start.
* Type connection-handle creation payloads with valid connectable entities.
* Define one shared destination contract for endpoint reconnection.
* Retain complete endpoint entities as frontend metadata.
* Ensure labels and connections are rejected as connection endpoints.
* Keep connection bend-point, connection-label, and endpoint-reconnect gestures as dedicated handlers.

h3. Tests and Linting

* Replace partial any fixtures with canonical entity factories.
* Add compile-time coverage for discriminated unions and endpoint exclusions.
* Retain integration coverage for selection and drag interactions.
* Enable no-explicit-any for the completed reusable canvas directory.

h2. Out of Scope

* Adding connector troubleshooting commands.
* Migrating the legacy flow-designer canvas.
* Changing REST endpoint behavior.
* Changing rendered appearance or interaction semantics.
* Dispatching page-specific state actions from the reusable component.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Every Canvas wrapper uses its canonical entity type.
* CanvasDatum and SelectionTarget are discriminated unions.
* Canvas collection inputs use concrete entity arrays.
* D3 renderer and layer contracts do not use explicit any.
* Drag and render callbacks have shared typed contracts.
* Connection creation and reconnection accept only valid connectable entities.
* Labels and connections are rejected as connection endpoints at compile time.
* Full endpoint entities remain frontend metadata and are not added to REST payloads.
* Context-menu and selection behavior remains unchanged.
* Drag, bend-point, label, resize, and reconnect behavior remains unchanged.
* no-explicit-any is enabled for the reusable canvas directory.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, integration tests, and production build pass.

summary: Add connector troubleshooting actions and state presentation
description:
h2. Background

The NiFi backend exposes a TROUBLESHOOTING connector state and connector actions for entering and ending that state. The frontend does not currently recognize the state or present the corresponding actions.

Users need an explicit, permission-aware way to start and end troubleshooting and a consistent visual representation of the active state.

h2. Goals

* Add TROUBLESHOOTING to the frontend connector state model.
* Add ENTER_TROUBLESHOOTING and END_TROUBLESHOOTING action names.
* Display troubleshooting actions only when allowed by the backend.
* Execute troubleshooting lifecycle requests through connector state effects.
* Present the troubleshooting state consistently in connector listings and details.

h2. Scope

h3. Shared Connector Contracts

* Add TROUBLESHOOTING to ConnectorState.
* Add ENTER_TROUBLESHOOTING and END_TROUBLESHOOTING to ConnectorActionName.
* Add a shared isConnectorInTroubleshooting utility.
* Map TROUBLESHOOTING to the caution status variant.
* Update connector permission and action-availability helpers.

h3. Connector Service and State

* Add service methods for entering and ending troubleshooting mode.
* Add connector state actions for both lifecycle operations.
* Add effects that invoke the service and process successful responses.
* Update connector entities from server responses rather than constructing local state transitions.
* Surface lifecycle failures through the existing connector error handling.
* Prevent duplicate requests while a lifecycle operation is already in progress.

summary: Add troubleshooting route guards, banners, and live state synchronization
description:
h2. Background

Advanced connector pages and canvas editing are valid only while a connector is in TROUBLESHOOTING. The frontend must enforce that requirement for direct navigation, clearly identify the active mode, and react when the connector state changes during an open session.

Without synchronized connector-state polling and route protection, users can remain on an editing page after troubleshooting ends or access an advanced route through a stale deep link.

h2. Goals

* Guard troubleshooting-only routes.
* Display a persistent troubleshooting banner on affected pages.
* Keep the current connector entity synchronized with backend state.
* Enable or disable canvas editing when troubleshooting starts or ends.
* Refresh affected data after troubleshooting ends.
* Fail closed when connector state cannot be confirmed.

h2. Scope

h3. Troubleshooting Route Guard

* Add a functional route guard for troubleshooting-only connector routes.
* Read the connector identifier and process-group identifier from inherited route parameters.
* Use a matching connector entity from state when available.
* Fetch the connector entity when state is missing or belongs to another connector.
* Allow activation only when the connector is in TROUBLESHOOTING.
* Return a UrlTree redirect instead of cancelling navigation.
* Support contextual redirect destinations for canvas and Controller Service routes.
* Redirect safely when route parameters are missing or the connector request fails.
* Store a successfully fetched connector entity for downstream resolvers and components.

h3. Guarded Routes

Apply the guard to advanced editing routes, including:

* Processor advanced UI.
* Controller Service advanced UI.
* Future per-component editing routes that require troubleshooting mode.

Each guarded route must declare the appropriate in-context redirect destination.

h3. Troubleshooting Banners

* Display a non-dismissible caution banner on the connector canvas while troubleshooting is active.
* Display the same troubleshooting context on the connector-scoped Controller Services page.
* Explain that changes are limited to the troubleshooting session and may be reverted when the session ends.
* Hide the banner outside troubleshooting mode.
* Preserve existing error-banner behavior.

h3. Connector Entity Synchronization

* Load the connector entity when the connector canvas initializes.
* Refresh the connector entity alongside connector flow polling.
* Start connector-entity polling on sibling advanced pages where the canvas is not mounted.
* Stop polling when the page is destroyed.
* Avoid duplicate polling loops and stale cross-connector state.

h3. State Transition Handling

React to connector state edges for the same connector:

* Initial load: configure canvas editing from the current connector state.
* Enter troubleshooting: enable editing without unnecessarily reloading the flow.
* End troubleshooting: disable editing, reload the current flow, and show confirmation.
* Steady state: avoid redundant state updates while correcting any canvas configuration drift.
* Connector change: treat the new connector as an initial load instead of a troubleshooting transition.

User-driven refresh after ending troubleshooting must not be dropped by polling throttles.

h3. Tests

Add coverage for:

* Warm-state guard activation.
* Cold deep-link connector loading.
* Redirects for non-troubleshooting connectors.
* Context-specific redirect destinations.
* Missing route parameters.
* Connector loading failures.
* Banner visibility.
* Initial editing configuration.
* Enter and end transition edges.
* Flow reload after ending troubleshooting.
* Cross-connector navigation.
* Polling startup, refresh, and teardown.
* Avoidance of redundant steady-state updates.

h2. Out of Scope

* Component run-status operations.
* Processor advanced UI implementation.
* Controller Service mutation operations.
* Alignment, Remote Process Group refresh, and provenance replay.
* Changes to backend troubleshooting lifecycle behavior.
* Changes to connector action availability.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Troubleshooting-only routes cannot activate unless the connector is in TROUBLESHOOTING.
* Cold deep links validate connector state through one backend request.
* Denied navigation redirects to the appropriate canvas or Controller Services page.
* Connector loading failures deny access and surface through existing error handling.
* The connector canvas and Controller Services page display a troubleshooting banner only while the mode is active.
* Canvas editing is enabled only while troubleshooting is active.
* Ending troubleshooting disables editing and refreshes the current flow.
* Connector state polling keeps open pages synchronized with backend changes.
* Polling stops when the owning page is destroyed.
* Cross-connector navigation does not produce false enter or exit transitions.
* Existing selection, navigation, polling, and error behavior remains unchanged.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, and production build pass.

summary: Add connector canvas component operations and processor advanced UI access
description:
h2. Background

Troubleshooting mode requires controlled component operations on the connector's managed process group. The connector canvas currently lacks the command layer, operation panel, and processor advanced UI navigation needed to diagnose and correct component-level problems.

These operations must respect connector state, component state, permissions, selection, and revision handling.

h2. Goals

* Add troubleshooting-only component run-status operations.
* Provide a reusable operation panel for single, multi, and empty selections.
* Centralize connector canvas command dispatch.
* Keep returned component entities synchronized with connector canvas state.
* Allow access to processor advanced UI when supported.
* Preserve permission and connector-state boundaries.

h2. Scope

h3. Component Commands

Support the following operations:

* Start selected components.
* Stop selected components.
* Enable selected components.
* Disable selected components.
* Run a single processor once.
* Terminate threads for a single processor.
* Start, stop, enable, or disable the current process group when no components are selected.

Introduce a connector canvas command service that converts selected canvas targets into typed requests and dispatches the corresponding state actions.

h3. Operation Eligibility

Determine operation availability from:

* Connector troubleshooting state.
* Component type.
* Component run state.
* Component permissions.
* Operate permissions.
* Current selection count.
* Current process-group permissions.
* Whether a component is already being updated.

Use shared pure utilities so context menus and the operation panel apply identical eligibility rules.

h3. Operation Panel

Add a reusable operation control that:

* Reflects the current canvas selection.
* Shows only operations valid for the complete selection.
* Supports current-process-group operations for an empty selection.
* Distinguishes single-component-only operations.
* Displays saving or disabled treatment while requests are active.
* Emits user intent without directly owning page-specific state.

h3. State and Effects

* Add typed actions and effects for run-status operations.
* Preserve each component's current revision in requests.
* Update connector canvas collections with returned entities.
* Apply revision-aware updates so stale responses do not replace newer state.
* Mark affected components as saving while requests are active.
* Clear saving state on success and failure.
* Surface errors through the connector error context.
* Reload or reconcile state when an operation cannot be safely applied locally.

h3. Context Menu Integration

* Add troubleshooting-only component operations to the connector canvas context menu.
* Use the same eligibility utilities as the operation panel.
* Keep read-only actions available outside troubleshooting where appropriate.
* Do not expose mutation commands outside troubleshooting mode.

h3. Processor Advanced UI

* Add a context-menu action for processors that advertise advanced UI support.
* Load the required extension-type metadata when the connector canvas initializes.
* Add a processor advanced UI route under the connector canvas.
* Protect the route with the troubleshooting-state guard.
* Resolve the connector, process-group, and processor parameters required by the advanced UI.
* Return users to the connector canvas after closing or when activation is denied.
* Surface resolver and loading failures through existing error handling.

h3. Tests

Add coverage for:

* Operation eligibility by component type, state, and permissions.
* Single, multi, and empty selections.
* Current-process-group operations.
* Run-once and terminate-thread restrictions.
* Typed request construction and revision handling.
* Saving-state lifecycle.
* Success, failure, and stale-response handling.
* Context-menu and operation-panel consistency.
* Advanced UI action visibility.
* Advanced UI parameter resolution.
* Route protection and back navigation.
* Missing extension metadata and unsupported processors.

h2. Out of Scope

* Connector-scoped Controller Service mutation operations.
* Remote Process Group refresh.
* Alignment commands.
* Provenance replay.
* General component configuration editing.
* Changes to backend component operation semantics.
* Operations on the legacy flow-designer canvas.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Mutation commands are available only while the connector is in TROUBLESHOOTING.
* Start, stop, enable, and disable work for valid single and multi-selections.
* Empty-selection operations target the current process group.
* Run once and terminate threads are restricted to one eligible processor.
* Context menus and the operation panel calculate identical operation availability.
* Requests contain the correct component identifiers, types, and revisions.
* Successful responses update the correct typed entity collections.
* Stale responses do not overwrite newer entity revisions.
* Saving state is applied and cleared for all affected components.
* Failures surface through existing connector error handling.
* Supported processors can open their advanced UI from the connector canvas.
* Unsupported processors do not expose the advanced UI action.
* Advanced UI routes require active troubleshooting mode.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, and production build pass.

summary: Enable connector-scoped Controller Service management during troubleshooting
description:
h2. Background

The connector-scoped Controller Services page is currently read-only. During troubleshooting, users need to create and manage Controller Services within the connector's managed process-group hierarchy.

Outside troubleshooting mode, the page must remain read-only. All mutations must use connector-scoped APIs and respect process-group permissions, service ownership, dependencies, and revision handling.

h2. Goals

* Make connector-scoped Controller Services editable during troubleshooting.
* Preserve read-only inspection outside troubleshooting.
* Support the complete Controller Service management lifecycle.
* Use connector-scoped service APIs and state.
* Enforce process-group and component permissions.
* Keep state synchronized after each mutation.

h2. Scope

h3. Page Behavior

* Determine editability from the current connector's troubleshooting state.
* Pass readOnly=false to the Controller Service table only while troubleshooting.
* Preserve read-only configuration viewing outside troubleshooting.
* Show the New Controller Service action only when troubleshooting is active and the current process group is writable.
* Respect whether a service is defined in the current group or inherited from an ancestor.
* Prevent modification of inherited membership from the wrong process-group scope.

h3. Supported Operations

Add troubleshooting support for:

* Create Controller Service.
* Configure Controller Service.
* Enable Controller Service.
* Disable Controller Service.
* Change Controller Service version.
* Delete Controller Service.
* Clear Controller Service bulletins.

* Reuse the established Controller Service dialogs and request contracts.

* Track the service currently being saved or deleted.
* Update or reload the Controller Service collection after successful operations.
* Clear saving state on both success and failure.
* Surface failures through the Controller Services error context.
* Prevent overlapping mutations for the same service.

h3. Service Scope and Permissions

* Require active troubleshooting for mutations.
* Require write permission on the applicable process group or service.

* Do not expose access-policy management when the connector scope does not support it.

h3. Advanced UI

h3. Tests

Add coverage for:

* Editable behavior during troubleshooting.

* Current-group and inherited-service permissions.
* Create, configure, enable, disable, version-change, delete, and bulletin-clear actions.
* Saving-state lifecycle.
* Success and failure effects.
* Collection reconciliation after mutation.
* Advanced UI route protection and parameter resolution.
* Unsupported advanced UI.
* Connector entity polling while the page is mounted.

h2. Out of Scope

* Alignment commands.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* The Controller Services page remains read-only outside TROUBLESHOOTING.
* The page becomes editable only while troubleshooting is active.

summary: Add alignment, Remote Process Group refresh, and provenance replay to connector troubleshooting
description:
h2. Background

Several diagnostic and layout operations remain unavailable on the connector canvas during troubleshooting. Users need to align selected components, refresh Remote Process Group metadata, and replay eligible provenance events without leaving the connector context.

These operations must be available only while troubleshooting is active and must preserve permissions, revisions, polling safety, and error handling.

h2. Goals

* Add horizontal and vertical alignment for selected canvas components.
* Add asynchronous Remote Process Group refresh.
* Allow provenance replay only during troubleshooting.
* Integrate these operations with connector canvas commands, context menus, state, and effects.
* Preserve existing read-only behavior outside troubleshooting.

h2. Scope

h3. Component Alignment

* Add an Align context-menu submenu with horizontal and vertical options.
* Show alignment actions only while canvas editing is enabled.
* Require at least two eligible positionable components.
* Exclude connections and unsupported selections.
* Calculate target positions from the selected components' visual bounds.
* Preserve each component's current revision.
* Dispatch one typed bulk-position update.
* Update attached connection geometry consistently where required.
* Reuse the existing bulk position persistence and failure-recovery behavior.

Horizontal alignment centers selected components on the selection's Y-axis center line.

Vertical alignment centers selected components on the selection's X-axis center line.

h3. Remote Process Group Refresh

* Add Refresh remote to the context menu for eligible Remote Process Groups.
* Require active troubleshooting, read permission, and a known flow-refreshed timestamp.
* Start the refresh through the connector-scoped API.
* Store the Remote Process Group identifier and original refresh timestamp.
* Poll until the returned flow-refreshed timestamp changes.
* Display temporary refreshing state while polling.
* Replace the Remote Process Group entity with the refreshed response.
* Reload related connections after completion when endpoint metadata may have changed.
* Stop polling on completion, error, navigation, canvas reset, or explicit teardown.
* Prevent multiple polling intervals from running for the same refresh session.

h3. Provenance Replay

* Propagate whether replay is allowed from the current connector troubleshooting state.
* Allow replay only when both conditions are true:
** The provenance event reports replayAvailable.
** The connector is currently in TROUBLESHOOTING.
* Apply the same replay gating to provenance preview and full provenance listing flows.
* Preserve connector canvas back navigation.
* Submit replay using the event identifier and cluster node identifier.
* Display confirmation after successful submission.
* Surface replay failures through existing error handling.
* Hide or disable replay outside troubleshooting mode.

h3. State and Effects

* Add typed actions and state for Remote Process Group refresh details and polling status.
* Add selectors for the active refresh session.
* Add alignment command dispatch through the connector canvas command layer.
* Ensure refresh responses cannot update a later or unrelated canvas session.
* Clear refresh state during canvas reset.
* Preserve immutable collection updates.

h3. Tests

Add coverage for:

* Alignment visibility and eligibility.
* Horizontal and vertical target calculations.
* Mixed and unsupported selections.
* Revision-preserving bulk updates.
* Remote Process Group refresh visibility and permissions.
* Polling startup, repeated ticks, completion, failure, and teardown.
* Duplicate polling-start protection.
* Stale refresh-session isolation.
* Related connection reload after refresh.
* Provenance replay availability during troubleshooting.
* Replay suppression outside troubleshooting.
* Replay success and failure behavior.
* Back-navigation preservation.

h2. Out of Scope

* General component run-status operations.
* Processor advanced UI.
* Controller Service management.
* Changes to Remote Process Group backend refresh semantics.
* Changes to provenance replay backend semantics.
* Alignment on the legacy flow-designer canvas.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Horizontal and vertical alignment are available only for valid troubleshooting selections.
* Alignment requests preserve component identifiers, types, positions, and revisions.
* Unsupported selections do not expose alignment actions.
* Eligible Remote Process Groups expose Refresh remote during troubleshooting.
* Refresh polling stops when the flow-refreshed timestamp changes.
* Only one polling interval remains active for a refresh session.
* Polling and in-flight requests stop when the canvas is reset or destroyed.
* Refreshed entities and related connections are reconciled with state.
* Provenance replay is available only when the event is replayable and troubleshooting is active.
* Replay is unavailable outside troubleshooting even when the event reports replayAvailable.
* Success and failure feedback uses existing application mechanisms.
* Frontend lint, strict type-check, unit tests, and production build pass.

summary: Provide connector-scoped access to managed Process Group configuration
description:
Process Groups managed by a Connector cannot be retrieved through the standard Process Group REST resource unless the Connector is in Troubleshooting mode.

This restriction is intentional for general component operations: connector-managed flow components should not be directly accessible while the Connector owns and manages its flow. However, it also prevents clients with read access to the Connector from retrieving the configuration of a managed Process Group for read-only inspection.

The Connector REST resource currently exposes:

* Connector flow retrieval, returning a ProcessGroupFlowEntity containing canvas contents and breadcrumb information
* Connector-scoped retrieval of individual Controller Services
* Connector-scoped status and status-history operations for managed Process Groups

It does not expose an equivalent operation that returns a complete ProcessGroupEntity. A ProcessGroupFlowEntity does not contain all Process Group configuration fields, permissions, and revision information needed by clients that display Process Group configuration.

Consequently, clients must either:

1. Use the standard Process Group endpoint, which fails while the Connector is not in Troubleshooting mode
2. Work with an incomplete representation from the Connector flow endpoint
3. Require Troubleshooting mode merely to inspect configuration, even though no modification is being requested

A client with read access to a Connector should be able to retrieve the complete configuration entity for a Process Group belonging to that Connector’s managed flow, regardless of whether the Connector is in Troubleshooting mode. This capability must not make unrelated Process Groups accessible through the Connector or weaken the existing restrictions on standard Process Group operations.

summary: Avoid sanitizing nonexistent connection positions in canvas flow snapshots
description:
h2. Background

Canvas connections do not have a position. Their canvas geometry is represented by bends and labelIndex.

The connector canvas flow sanitizer currently passes connection.position to sanitizePosition(). Because connection.position is normally undefined, every connection is incorrectly treated as having a corrupt position.

The flow-designer sanitizer contains the same behavior.

h2. Current Behavior

Loading a connector canvas logs a warning for each connection:

{code}
Component Connection 106a6c6f-60ea-3aec-8544-f279243aafe3 has an out-of-range position undefined — falling back to (0, 0). Drag the component to a new location and save to repair the persisted value.
{code}

The warning is misleading:

* The persisted connection is not corrupt.
* Connections cannot be repaired by dragging them to a new position.
* The sanitizer adds an artificial position of (0, 0) to a non-positionable entity.

h2. Root Cause

The connection-specific sanitizer currently performs both of these operations:

* Sanitizes entity.position.
* Sanitizes component.bends.

Connections should only have their bend coordinates sanitized.

The affected paths are:

* apps/nifi/src/app/pages/connectors/state/connector-canvas/connector-canvas.effects.ts
* apps/nifi/src/app/pages/flow-designer/state/flow/flow.effects.ts

h2. Expected Behavior

* Connection entities are not passed through position sanitization.
* Connection bend coordinates continue to be sanitized.
* Loading a valid connection without position does not log a warning.
* Positionable canvas components continue to receive the existing position validation.

h2. Implementation Notes

Connections do not have a singular position property. Their canvas geometry is determined by their endpoints and bend coordinates, while labelIndex identifies the segment used for label placement.

The sanitizer should validate each bend coordinate without attempting to validate or add connection.position.

The same correction is required in both the connector canvas and flow-designer ingestion paths.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Connector canvas does not call sanitizePosition() for connection.position.
* Flow designer does not call sanitizePosition() for connection.position.
* Connection bends remain protected against non-finite and out-of-range coordinates.
* Valid connections without position produce no console warning.
* Invalid connection bends are replaced with the fallback coordinate and emit the expected warning.
* Unit tests cover positionless connections and invalid connection bends in both canvas paths.
* Existing position sanitization tests for processors, ports, funnels, labels, process groups, and remote process groups continue to pass.
* Frontend lint, unit tests, and production build pass.

LogMessage drops message when log level is below logback allowed
description: When using the LogMessage processor, if a message is configured to log at a level that is below what is set in logback.xml (for example logging at "info" when the default log level is "warn"), the message doesn't get logged {-}and an error is thrown because the flowfile is unable to be routed to failure (the only available route on the processor is Success){-}. Since this is a user configurable log level for a specific case, the level for the message should be able to override the global log level in logback.xml so as to avoid this behavior.

summary: TransformXML Documentation doesn't explain usage of dynamic properties in stylesheets
description:
In the TransformXML Documentation there is a section on Dynamic Properties. It says:

"These XSLT parameters are passed to the transformer."

There is no mention on how to use the parameters in a XSLT. Maybe go to add this information to this section:

From the Saxon documentation:

 

These parameters are accessible within the stylesheet as normal variables, using the {{$name}} syntax, provided they are declared using a top-level {{xsl:param}} element. If there is no such declaration, the supplied parameter value is silently ignored.

If the {{xsl:param}} element has an {{as}} attribute indicating the required type, then the string value supplied on the command line is cast to this type: this may result in an error, for example if an integer is required and the supplied value cannot be converted to an integer. If the parameter is declared with the option {{static="yes"}} (new in XSLT 3.0) then the value is supplied as a static parameter value.

 

Example:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="2.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" >

    <xsl:output method="xml"/>

    <xsl:param name = "parameterName" />

    <xsl:template match="/">
        <hdr:messageId><xsl:value-of select="$parameterName"/></hdr:messageId>                                
    </xsl:template>    
    
</xsl:stylesheet>
